facts: A non-empty submitted line reaches processInputWordAnalyze.
A retail command requiring subtarget selection saves its raw line and later calls executeTextCommand again with the selected actor.
The debug test precedes ordinary parsing.
Each invocation calls _parseTextCommand once.
Parser success reaches local command execution; parser failure calls chat with the original raw line and returns false.
The callee-clean implementation receives one 32-bit Lua argument-container pointer and returns with RET 4.
Argument variant extraction yields the borrowed narrow string pointer passed to the parser thunk.
Parser failure becomes nil Lua-visible results; parser success becomes the parsed command tuple.
The core is __thiscall-shaped: bool parse(TextCommandParser* this, const char* input, ParsedCommand* output), with ECX plus two stack arguments and RET 8.
It checks the first narrow byte for slash and returns success in AL.
It writes the caller-owned 16-byte output only on success. Exact source types beyond these bounded roles are not claimed.
MyPlayer slot 42 is reached only after Lua accepts parser output.
A parser-declined custom line cannot reach this function.
chat resets temporary chat mode, validates the input, converts pronouns, and calls _chat.
The registered _chat receives the converted message rather than the original raw submitted bytes.
Registration function 0x00743D80 passes 0x006DE7D0 to its generic binder while registering literal _chat.
The thunk dispatches ECX vtable byte offset 0x10C, slot 67; the MyPlayer vtable entry resolves to 0x006E91F0.

Slot 67 is void __thiscall-shaped as void PlayerBase::chat(ExecuteParameters const&) const, with ECX plus one stack argument and RET 4. It extracts two 16-byte Lua values, branches on chat mode, and then invokes channel-specific builders.
Returning at the thunk before its tail jump is before builder construction and queueing. No slot-67 local object has yet been constructed.

vtableFacts: All three classes have 12-slot vtables. Slots 2, 3, and 4 dispatch _onCommandRejected, _onPreCommand, and _onPostCommand.
CommandBlock slot 10 fires _onCommandRequest and slot 11 fires _onCommandCancel; CommandNonBlock slot 10 fires _onCommandEvent and slot 11 fires _onCommandCancel.
The cancel wrappers read whether their fifth argument equals global 0x01355294 and expose that comparison as a Lua boolean; they do not store a handled result.
executionState: ExecutionClientSideBlockEvent+0x1D is an abort latch, +0x20 is a server-order marker, +0x21 is an armed flag, and +0x28 is a pending checker.

The pre callback runs before +0x21 is armed; cancellation later invokes slot 11 and may clear +0x21 before post notification. These fields govern an already-created event lifecycle, not text parse-or-chat routing.
lifecycleCancellation.reason: Every recovered fire site is a void callback dispatch. No callback return, shared text-command handled bit, or later execute-versus-chat branch was found. _onCommandCancel reports cleanup after event cancellation and receives no complete submitted raw line.

strongestCandidate.name: top-level command-definition lookup interception
strongestCandidate.boundary: Detour 0x0056D3C0 on the exact pinned build and dispatch only calls returning to 0x0056E6A4.
strongestCandidate.evidenceLimit: Static analysis establishes the lookup ABI and eligible caller. A 2026-09-07 live probe proved /pos dispatch and visible toggle; preservation rows and exact per-submit hit count remain unverified.

callingConventionAndPrototype: int __thiscall lookup(TextCommandParser* this, const CommandToken* token, void* auxiliaryOutput); callee RET 8
candidateVerdicts.inputEncoding: The token first field is a borrowed narrow NUL-terminated byte pointer. Exact character encoding is unresolved; addon recognition is limited to an ASCII slash prefix and ASCII command name.
candidateVerdicts.inputOwnershipAndLifetime: Retail owns the token and auxiliary output. The addon may inspect token bytes only for the call duration and must copy retained bytes.
candidateVerdicts.expectedInvocationThread: The 2026-09-07 live probe observed lookup and addon dispatch on one OS thread. Broader UI-thread identity is not established.
candidateVerdicts.exactOnceBehavior: The live aggregate contained two eligible lookup entries and two addon dispatches across the user test. The probe did not isolate the number of physical submissions, so exact once-per-submit behavior remains unverified.
candidateVerdicts.consumeForwardMechanism: For an addon-handled ASCII command, leave auxiliary output untouched and return the retail miss sentinel -2 without calling the original lookup. Forward every ineligible caller and unhandled token to the original trampoline unchanged.
candidateVerdicts.cleanupObligations: Retain no token or pending state. Catch addon exceptions and forward the original lookup unchanged.
candidateVerdicts.unsupportedBuildBehavior: Require exact executable size and SHA-256, the exact VA, and one executable-section signature match. If any gate fails, expose no command callback.
candidateVerdicts.evidence: Static caller analysis identifies the top-level lookup return at 0x0056E6A4. On 2026-09-07, live retail diagnostics recorded two lookup entries, recognitions, handled dispatches, and synthetic misses with zero forwards; /pos visibly toggled the Position window. No _chat thunk entry occurred.

proposedHookContract.install: Install the lookup detour only after exact executable identity, exact address, and unique signature gates pass.
lookupHook: Forward calls from every return address except 0x0056E6A4 without inspecting the token.
At the eligible caller, inspect only the borrowed token first-field byte pointer for an exact ASCII addon command.
If handled, leave auxiliary output untouched and return -2 without invoking the original lookup.
If unhandled or addon dispatch fails, call the original lookup with the original ECX, token, and auxiliary-output pointers and preserve its result.
preservation: Ordinary chat, known retail commands, unknown slash commands, retail macros, and deferred retail commands use original code unless the extension explicitly handles its own ASCII command.
Do not fabricate a retail command id, retain token state, alter packet data, or hook chat, WndProc, keyboard input, builders, or queue forwarders.
proposedHookContract.knownLimit: Live validation proved /pos toggling but did not isolate exact hits per physical submission or execute the four unhandled preservation rows.
